FINAL SUBMISSION

**What is submitted:** `/work/edited` is empty — the model's weights are unchanged from the starting weights (which include the one inherited earlier edit). I did not find, meet or beat an edit that genuinely improves accuracy, and every edit I tested measured strictly worse or noise-equal, so shipping them would risk a score below zero.

**What I measured (all runs on this session's practice problems, paired `model: "both"` generation):**
- Starting weights: 45.3% baseline accuracy (40.1% MATH / 60.9% GSM8K per SUMMARY.txt); 28.5% of outputs truncated at 8,192 tokens (0% correct on those); 63.4% correctness among finishers. On the 512 select generations I reproduced 49.0% accuracy with 28.1% truncation; correct finishes are short (~1,957 tokens, ~2 `</think>` tags); 124/512 outputs stream 5+ `</think>` at only 7.3% accuracy — the dominant failure, induced by the inherited prior edit amplifying the `</think>` readout at "Wait-loop"-like positions (which also fires at ordinary answer-section positions measured by teacher forcing).
- Mechanism: difference-of-means probes separate thinking vs answer-section MLP activations at every layer, but the direction is a shift not a gate (uniformly negative projection in the MLP space). Any rank-one residual edit along this axis (additive or "suppressing") boosts `</think>` everywhere and tips the temp-0.6/top-k-20/presence-penalty-1.5 sampler into an infinite single-token storm the model cannot escape. DLA at the problem near-tie positions is fully distributed (no single unit; top contributors |Δ|<4 per layer). A TF pass showed the broken distributions reach p(</think>)≈1 from token 1 (mean logprob −0.85 → −9.28 for the same text).
- Tested edits vs baseline (paired, original from cache): gen_3 (−10.94pp, cut 36→59%), gen_4 (−43.75pp), gen_5 (−43.75pp), gen_7 (−43.75pp), gen_11 (+1.56pp but worse cut rate), gen_10 (ablate top-DLA think-promoter down_proj columns L23:474/40/1549, L22:26/11/351, L19:31, L21:18/139, L15:54 — best candidate, but across all 573 graded gens of select+confirm_1+confirm_2: original 281 correct vs edited 280 correct, flips 57→58; no-boxed rate rose +6–12pp; confirm_2 was −7.81pp on one half), gen_17 (L20:752 column ×2, −1.56pp). Control gen_9 (saving identical tensors) scored 0.0pp with 4/4 flips both ways = pure GPU noise, and confirmed save_edit replaces (not adds) weights.
- Conclusion: essentially no headroom for residual-axis edits on this model; the inherited edit holds the generation equilibrium on a knife-edge that any measured perturbation breaks.

**Evidence strength:** base rates reproduce in two independent split halves (select) and four confirmation halves (confirm_1, confirm_2 used strictly for confirmation, never for choosing); the one promising candidate (gen_10) failed to replicate: net −1 correct across 510 problems, so I rejected it per the pre-set rule (confirm drift < 0 → ship original).

**What would help if I had more budget:** dense teacher-forced measurement across hundreds of full-length outputs to (a) build a proper gate (not a shift) for the answer region, or (b) identify a per-unit/neuron across layers that suppressing is safe — my TF data was limited (activations cost ~3 GiB per pass) and every single-hypothesis edit I constructed collapsed. Anything claimed fine-grained here is unproven.

Notes with all numbers, flips and the exact edit table are in `/work/notes.md`.
